# Cluaiz Engine Runtime & Host (`engine/runtime`)

Model execution supervisor with separate chat, ONNX-task and GGUF-speech owners.

## Speech admission and shared load transitions

The API uses `SpeechHost` admission for both TTS backends; overlapping requests return `speech_busy`. Preparation and backend-release workers keep a cloned lease if their caller disconnects, so prepared speech references do not accumulate behind an unbounded native queue. Chat/STT generation is independent. Only load decisions/allocations share `EngineHost::model_transition`, not all inference.

GGUF load identity includes relevant captured settings and backbone/projector path, size and mtime; CPU selection also disables operation/KV/projector GPU offload. ONNX TTS admission counts the complete installed package, with the same configurable media workspace/reserve policy. Live checks and estimates do not reserve OS memory or establish native peak usage.

`speech_plan.rs` composes the same complete-package host check with the existing tensor/KV `Planner`. Codec GPU weights/workspace are subtracted from the live device snapshot before planning the backbone; codec CPU is the next option. The selected backbone may use partial GPU layers independently of codec placement. Speech keeps its existing 4096 context, 512 batch and F16 KV. Explicit CPU stays CPU; explicit GPU overcommit is refused even though the generic manual planner permits it. Auto driver-load failure rechecks CPU admission before retrying. Logs show selected flags and estimated bytes; these are not measured allocations or a realtime promise. A retained owner changes placement after a relevant settings change or unload/reload, not merely because another application frees VRAM.

Switching to GGUF releases only an ONNX `text_to_speech` resident, preserving an STT/embedding resident. Switching to ONNX TTS releases the GGUF speech resident. Chat remains loaded. The voices API exposes independent languages, explicit/automatic language control, reference mode and coherent-input guidance without loading inference sessions.

## GGUF speech retention

`speech_host.rs` serializes generation and native destruction behind one mutex. Each request replaces the resident's lease identity, including requests for the same model, so an old timer cannot unload a newer request or replacement. Timers weakly reference the owner and do not extend the host lifetime. Positive minutes start after successful generation; failures and keep_alive0release the resident. The native handles stay on the blocking side. Reference source authorization/decoding happens in the shared API media path before dispatch. New native PCM deltas, after shared tempo, become bounded `AudioEvent::Chunk` WAV data URIs through the existing backpressured channel, followed by the complete encoded utterance. Nonstreaming consumers ignore parts and await completion. A closed receiver cancels queued work before load and active work at prompt/frame boundaries; native load and an individual native step remain non-preemptible. Earlier valid chunks can precede a later error; no successful final event is fabricated.

## Architecture

## Components

## Media availability contract

- **Inputs:** `resolve_support` accepts package evidence, actually wired backend inputs, an optional trusted loaded model/projector pairing and enabled attachment routes. That pairing cannot be deserialized from a user request.
- **Planning:** `EngineHost::input_support` reads session/model state without waiting behind generation. A busy or different selected model remains unverified; another model's loaded encoder flags do not redefine this selected model's support. `media_support` adds attachment descriptors after releasing those locks, using the same resolver. The Chat planner presents one concise input contract and keeps the full internal evidence private.
- **Output:** intrinsic `inputs`, effective `available_inputs`, per-input `model_support`/`available`/`reason` and deduplicated usable attachment formats. Missing, ambiguous or incompatible assets, missing encoder, unwired dispatch and unverified pairing have distinct reasons.
- **Current route:** `CURRENT_NATIVE_CHAT_INPUTS` lists text/image/audio. `dispatch_prepared` owns decoded buffers through its blocking worker, checks the selected load fingerprint, probes package declarations and lazily loads the compatible projector before native generation. `dispatch_stream` retains the legacy text entry; API text uses `dispatch_chat_text` with selected-model identity and per-request cancellation.
- **Validation:** model and projector paths are canonicalized before comparing the trusted pairing, including Windows extended-path representation. Metadata alone never sets an image/audio input available. Unknown model capability is not promoted to support.
- **Scope:** the pure resolver reports availability; `EngineHost::media_support` supplies actual loaded encoder/pairing evidence. Decoder-library descriptors supply attachment extensions. Before lazy initialization, declared image/audio inputs can have `projector_pairing_unverified`; after initialization, reporting follows the loaded encoder. Shared media prepares document text/OCR and sampled video frames for these existing native chat routes. Sampled frames are image inputs, not intrinsic temporal-model support. General ONNX generative chat remains unwired.

## Request ownership and failure behavior

- **Model transitions:** one transition mutex serializes native load/unload allocations and publication; generation uses the paired session mutex. Requests queued after a selected-model/configuration change fail with an error instead of running on the new model. Native pointers are private to the session.

## ONNX audio ownership

- **Boundary:** `EngineHost.onnx.dispatch` receives `OnnxModel`, `AudioTask`, typed `AudioInput`, STT options, captured settings and keep-alive minutes. It uses the selected ONNX graph and never invokes llama text generation. Audio and chat have separate native owners.
- **Package identity:** declared asset paths must resolve inside the selected package. An explicit primary ONNX graph and its known required helper/external files must be present. The existing `PackageCapabilities` inventory is reused before a lease/native load and again when a queued request begins. Registry metadata, listed asset stamps, package snapshots, task and provider settings form the reuse key. This is cache invalidation, not cryptographic integrity; snapshot traversal has a depth ceiling and does not follow directory symlinks.
- **Concurrency:** one blocking worker holds the audio mutex through load and execution. Old sessions are dropped before replacement. Decoded input is retained by the queued request; it is not fetched again inside the ONNX backend. Model switches do not publish partially loaded sessions.
- **Retention:** zero unloads the audio owner after execution; null/-1 retain it until replacement. Positive minutes schedule expiry after completion. A key and monotonically increasing request generation must still match when the timer runs; old timers cannot unload a newer request's resident session. Execution errors discard the failed resident owner. An incomplete package rejected before the lease does not unload the existing valid resident.
- **Output:** `AudioEvent::Chunk` carries real incremental STT text or completed ONNX speech parts when supported by the selected family. `Completed` carries a transcript or the complete TTS WAV data URI. Native/model failures are errors; earlier speech parts may precede a terminal error.
- **Limits:** a dropped output consumer stops at a supported callback boundary. Deep encoder interruption, cancellation latency inside one native step, process peak bounds, positive-GPU/other-OS execution and comprehensive multi-family quality remain unverified. Shared load admission coordinates decisions; it does not reserve all concurrent inference memory.

## Native request continuation and resource policy

- **Preparation admission:** Chat attachment requests acquire one per-host permit before model/media preparation. A second attachment request receives `media_busy` before reading/decoding its source, rather than growing a decoded waiting queue. Plain text chat bypasses this permit. The API context, owned preparation task and native worker share its lifetime, including document-to-text dispatch and tool continuations. Disconnect does not release admission while detached decoding/native work still owns buffers. This is a concurrency bound, not a memory reservation or a capacity guarantee; ONNX/audio/embedding admission remains separate.
- **Media history:** each media turn re-evaluates its full typed input; text-only prefix history is cleared and no synthetic prefix cache is returned. The existing text sampler/prefill remains the single generation implementation. Oversized media context fails explicitly; whole-message auto fitting remains pending.
- **Cancellation:** API chat callbacks use their own retained atomic flag. The legacy CLI entry retains its global cancellation source. A cancelled queued API request fails before encoding; an active request stops at callback/evaluation boundaries. Long native encode/decode operations have no newly certified immediate-abort latency.
- **Skip reasoning:** text, prepared attachments and tool continuations retain the same request-owned skip flag created before dispatch. The serialized worker binds it to `NativeSession` only for that generation and clears the binding on success or error. Another queued request keeps its own flag. The shared native token loop invokes the upstream reasoning sampler and continues the existing answer stream; skipping does not cancel or reload the model.
- **Budget:** `media_generation` derives retained input bytes from the prepared request instead of charging the entire configured ceiling. Projector file size remains the weight-estimate lower bound; `media.projector_workspace_bytes` remains a conservative non-zero workspace estimate. Before copying native bitmaps, the session checks additional conversion buffers against fresh free memory and the existing safety reserve. A decoded-size change does not change projector identity. An idle projector can be reclaimed under RAM pressure and admitted again without changing the loaded Chat model/plan. These checks are estimates, not OS reservations or measured native peaks; native driver allocation failure has no automatic CPU retry.
- **Observations:** optional shared processing reporters cross the serialized native worker separately from token strings. The shared source decoder reports reads/decodes; the native adapter reports actual encode slices and prefill batches. API observation queues are bounded and opt-in. The separate ONNX task transport has not been changed.
- **Delivery:** the worker sends its existing error token on failure. The API interprets it as an SSE error object or a non-success JSON response, clears stale generation telemetry and retains decoded media across tool continuation requests.

## GGUF embedding lease

- **Owner:** `embedding_host::EmbeddingHost` keeps a separate native embedding model/context, leaving chat KV and speech residency intact. It reuses `MediaAdmission`, the shared load-transition lock, live `Planner` feasibility and `host::native_load` parameter translation. Whole-sequence context/batch settings are captured by one helper shared with plan preview.
- **Identity:** selected entry, complete package asset snapshot and load-setting fingerprint determine reuse. This is a metadata identity check, not a cryptographic integrity guarantee.
- **Execution:** one blocking worker evaluates text batches in order, checks output bytes and preserves actual tokenizer counts. Dropping its async caller sets cancellation; the worker retains admission and stops between native operations. An in-flight load/evaluation is not preempted. Status probing uses a nonblocking lock.
- **Retention:** zero unloads after execution, negative-one retains until replacement, and positive minutes start after successful completion. Weak timers compare the latest request lease before unloading; an old timer cannot expire a newer lease. Failures release the embedding resident. Neither this owner nor its expiry timer unloads chat or speech.
- **Limits:** text-only compatible native sequence pooling; image requests remain ONNX. Unsupported native architectures and oversized sequences return errors. Admission/planning are estimates and concurrency bounds, not OS reservations or all-device memory/performance certification.

## ONNX task lease

- **Owner:** `OnnxModel` validates the selected package/primary/assets. `OnnxHost::with_engine` is the single serialized load/reuse/replace/error/unload implementation shared by audio dispatch and embedding batches.
- **TTS provider recovery:** Before any audio part is emitted, an observed missing-cuDNN or DirectML operator failure can release the failed GPU session and retry the same package once on CPU, after fresh CPU admission. Once output starts, or the receiver closes, failure propagates without replaying the utterance from the start. The effective CPU owner retains the requested package/settings key, so a retained session does not retry the failed GPU on every utterance. Original settings are unchanged. CPU execution can be slower; unrecognized failures, STT and embedding execution do not retry.
- **Identity:** resident reuse includes declared asset/config stamps, task and captured provider settings. The existing generation guard protects newer requests from old positive keep-alive timers. This is cache identity, not cryptographic file integrity.
- **Embedding:** `embed` sends typed text/RGB to a blocking worker and returns actual vector/token results. Its byte and graph errors propagate to the API. Audio and embedding replace each other's ONNX resident task; neither calls chat unload. Simultaneously loaded chat/ONNX memory scheduling remains separate work.

## ONNX readiness ownership

- **Evidence:** the resident records successful native task, standalone input, package identity and captured provider settings. `readiness` returns only matching evidence and never accepts a client's readiness claim.
- **Resolver:** `media_support::resolve_onnx_support` combines it with graph declarations, known helper presence and common decoder formats. Auxiliary text is not a standalone image-graph text route; unknown/unimplemented task routes stay unavailable.
- **Invalidation:** failure/replacement/expiry/zero retention removes the resident; changed helpers/settings invalidate old readiness. Inspection never loads a session to manufacture readiness. First valid tasks may lazily initialize the owner.

## More files

- [`chat_memory.rs`](src/chat_memory.rs): a chat's KV cache on disk (llama-server's `--slot-save-path`, managed per chat). After an answer the KV goes to `kv_cache/chats/<chat>.kv` with its media layout and a JSON record (`ChatMemoryRecord`); when the chat continues after another chat, a model reload or a restart, the KV is read back instead of processing the whole history again. A record carries the exact model, load key and KV type it was made with (`memory_key`), so another model or context never restores it. `usage()` reports the disk it takes (CEP `kv.status`).
- [`embedding_host.rs`](src/embedding_host.rs): a GGUF embedding model kept loaded on its own, apart from the chat model, with the planner's load parameters (`capture_settings`). `try_acquire` takes it for one request; `unload_idle` frees it when nothing uses it; `resident_model` says which one is loaded.
- [`media_room.rs`](src/media_room.rs): `MediaRoom`, the list of idle models of other kinds (ONNX, GGUF speech, GGUF embedding) that a model may free when memory is short for its load or request. A model in use is never freed (each owner frees only when its lock is free), and the chat model is never on the list.
- [`vram_use.rs`](src/vram_use.rs): what models really took on this machine's GPU (`cluaiz_plan::margin`), kept in `engine/vram_margins.json` (`load`, `save`, `forget_model`, `free_gb`) so a restart plans with it on the first load.
- [`load_history.rs`](src/load_history.rs): every chat-model load, refused load, failed load and unload, one JSON line each in `engine/load_history.jsonl` beside `vram_margins.json` (the newest 500): placement, VRAM planned and taken, llama.cpp attempts, why the first one failed, wall time, and why the load ran (`requested`, `remeasured`, `step_down`). Read with CEP [`models.load_history`](../../docs/api/cep/models/models/models.load_history.md). Ids, numbers and error text only, no chat content.
- [`load_events.rs`](src/load_events.rs): the live view of a load while it runs: started (with the plan), each step from `llama_engine::native::load_steps` (weights read in percent, a llama.cpp fallback, context, warmup), a retry in a smaller placement, how it ended, and unloads. A broadcast channel (`subscribe`); nobody listening costs nothing. The API makes them `models.load` task progress and Engine events (`model.load_started` … `model.unloaded`); the CLI draws them on its loading line.

### Load retries

`EngineHost` loads the planned placement. When llama.cpp cannot load it for lack of memory (its error line says it could not allocate, or it gives no reason), `Planner::after_failed_load` records the miss and returns the next placement, which is loaded; at most three loads in all (`MAX_LOAD_ATTEMPTS` in `host.rs`), and each retry measures what it takes from the VRAM free right before it. After the first load the weight file is in the system's file cache, so a retry takes seconds, not the minute or more of a first read from a slow disk. llama.cpp's own fallbacks inside one load (fewer GPU layers, CPU only, without mmap or flash attention, in `engine/llama/src/native/core.rs`) still run inside an attempt and are shown as `fallback` steps. Any other failure (for example a drafter model that needs its main model: `dflash requires ctx_other to be set`) is not retried, since a smaller placement fails the same way. The error names every placement tried with llama.cpp's own last error line (`engine/llama/src/native/load_steps.rs`, `LoadFailure`).
